panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Apical four-chamber transthoracic echocardiogram from a patient with Ebstein anomaly, showing apically displaced tricuspid implantation, a small functional right ventricle, and right atrial dilation. B: Echocardiographic view demonstrating absent anterior tricuspid leaflet delamination with right atrial dilation, a characteristic manifestation of Ebstein anomaly; the leaflet abnormality is not explicitly represented in the allowed findings vocabulary.

It demonstrates apical displacement and tethering of the tricuspid leaflets, right atrial dilation, and the size of the functional RV. At the same time, color Doppler grades the severity of TR, and agitated saline contrast discloses interatrial shunting [8,17]. The diagnostic displacement is measured on the four-chamber view, relative to the anterior mitral leaflet. These features are illustrated in Figure 7, in which low tricuspid implantation, right atrial dilation, and absent leaflet delamination are evident.

plate_findings.evidence: Caption: "Globe-shaped cardiomegaly with indistinct great-vessel borders."

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Real chest radiograph with the characteristic globular cardiac silhouette and cardiomegaly described for Ebstein anomaly. B: Real chest radiograph demonstrating increased cardiothoracic ratio, a characteristic radiographic manifestation attributed by the disease-focused caption to Ebstein anomaly. C: Real chest radiograph explicitly showing the characteristic box-shaped cardiac silhouette and right atrial enlargement of Ebstein anomaly.
panels.attribution_text: Cueto-Robledo et al. Ebstein Anomaly: Imaging, Pathophysiology, and Therapeutics.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.112612. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 6.
panels.figure_caption: Chest radiographic findings. (A) Globe-shaped cardiomegaly with indistinct great-vessel borders. (B) Increased cardiothoracic ratio. (C) Box-shaped cardiac silhouette with right atrial enlargement, an appearance associated with a poorer prognosis when the cardiothoracic ratio exceeds 0.65.
in_text_mentions: Although it is not a diagnostic study, the chest radiograph is often the first abnormal investigation. Cardiomegaly with a globular or box-shaped silhouette is characteristic, and a cardiothoracic ratio above 0.65 is associated with a worse prognosis [31,32]. Representative radiographic appearances, including the box-shaped heart and progressive cardiomegaly, are shown in Figure 6.
